violations.message: Domain file src/modules/authentication/core/application/services/jwt-signer.service.ts imports from src/config/env-config.service.ts in application
Domain file src/modules/authentication/core/application/services/jwt-signer.service.ts imports from src/infrastructure/jwt/ports/jwks.port.ts in infrastructure
Domain class JwtSignerService holds infrastructure JwksPort via CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS (jwksService)

PaymentsTimeSeriesResponseDto.bucket hard-codes `enum: ['day', 'week']` and the type `'day' | 'week'` instead of using ANALYTICS_BUCKETS / AnalyticsBucket from analytics.policy. PaymentsTimeSeriesQueryDto uses those policy constants, so the bucket whitelist is now defined in two places and the two contracts can drift apart.

SeedDemoAuthUsersUseCase.seedUser has its own copy of the provisioning and rollback flow, and seeds a SUPER_ADMIN itself instead of sharing code with SeedSuperAdminUseCase. The copies already differ: it resets existing users, passes phone, and skips the password check.

SeedSuperAdminUseCase.execute repeats the user-provisioning saga from SeedDemoAuthUsersUseCase.seedUser: create identity, save credential with mustChangePassword, assign role, and roll back in reverse order. It also checks password length inline (< 6), a rule the other seeding path doesn't apply.

ChangePasswordDto.newPassword hardcodes the password minimum length (@MinLength(6) and Swagger minLength: 6). The same rule is repeated in RegisterDto.password, so the password policy is not defined in one place.
RegisterDto.password repeats the hardcoded password minimum length (@MinLength(6) and Swagger minLength: 6) that is also in ChangePasswordDto.newPassword. Move it to a shared constant or decorator.

The 'not found' handling for a failed ownership check and a missing user is copied here, and it differs from the other use cases: this file passes HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND explicitly and the others don't. This rule should live in one shared place.

This file declares its own DeleteAddressInput instead of using the command classes that the sibling use cases use. It also repeats the ownership and missing-user checks without the NOT_FOUND status and with the message 'User not found'.
This file declares its own SetDefaultAddressInput instead of using a command class. It also repeats the ownership and missing-user checks, and its handling differs from the add use case.
This file repeats the ownership and missing-user checks but leaves out the HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND that the add use case passes.
The role-code format regex /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/ on AssignRoleDto.roleCode is also in ListUsersQueryDto, with a different message. It should be defined once and reused.
ListUsersQueryDto.roleCode repeats the role-code regex from AssignRoleDto instead of using a shared definition.

UpdateAddressDto repeats every address field and validator from AddAddressDto instead of being derived from it (e.g. PartialType/OmitType). It also imports AddressType with an 'src/...' path, unlike the other address DTOs.
`amount` uses `@Min(0)`, while `ProcessRefundDto` and `RecordCodPaymentDto` use `@Min(0.01)`. The positive-amount rule is repeated with values that disagree.
The `status` filter is an unvalidated `string`, not `PaymentStatusType`. The page/limit bounds (min 1, max 100) appear only in Swagger metadata, with no `@Min`/`@Max` validators to enforce them.

`status` and `paymentMethod` are plain `string`, not the module's `PaymentStatusType`/`PaymentMethodType` used in `PaymentResponseDto`. It also repeats the payment read-model fields of `PaymentListItemResponseDto` and `PaymentResponseDto`, with different date types (string vs Date) and different optional/required fields.
`PaymentListItemResponseDto` repeats the payment read-model fields of `PaymentDetailResponseDto` instead of sharing them, and types `status`/`paymentMethod` as `string` instead of the module enums.

RegisterUserUseCase.execute maps failures to HTTP status codes (HttpStatus.CONFLICT, HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR from @nestjs/common). That is a transport/presentation (infrastructure) concern inside a file declared as domain.

This file is declared as domain, but `SetDefaultAddressUseCase.execute` does application-layer work. It checks caller access with `OwnedResourceAccessPolicy`, loads the user with `userRepository.findByIdForUpdate`, and saves with `userRepository.save(user, expectedVersion)`. The class is also marked with the NestJS `@Injectable()` decorator, which is framework wiring. Both responsibilities belong to the application layer, not domain.

CheckStockQueryDto is an HTTP transport contract: Swagger `@ApiPropertyOptional` documentation plus `@Type(() => Number)` query-string coercion. These responsibilities belong to the infrastructure (primary adapter/presentation) layer, not the declared application layer.

In class LowStockQueryDto, the @ApiPropertyOptional Swagger metadata and the @Type(() => Number) query-string conversion on threshold/page/limit are HTTP transport/presentation work, which belongs to infrastructure. They don't fit the application layer the file is assigned to.

CreatePaymentIntentUseCase.execute() does application work inside a file declared as domain: it calls the payment gateway (getGateway, createPaymentIntent), saves through the repository (paymentRepository.save), and maps errors to UseCaseError. The NestJS @Injectable() decorator adds framework wiring. These responsibilities belong to the application layer.
